chips.name: 8-bit Microprocessor
chips.story: The first chips that HCL used could run a single simple program at a time. Every transistor was visible under a basic microscope.
facts: About 8,500 transistors, a few thousand times fewer than a modern phone chip.
Fits one instruction per many clock ticks.

chips.name: 32-bit Processor
chips.story: Wider 32-bit data paths let computers handle bigger numbers and memory, the start of the desktop PC era.
facts: 32 data bits at once, four times the 8-bit chip.

chips.name: Superscalar Processor
chips.story: Superscalar designs could start more than one instruction per tick, so the chip did more work at the same speed.
facts: Power use climbs as speed grows, so heat becomes a design problem.

chips.name: Gigahertz-Class CPU
chips.story: Clock speeds crossed one billion ticks per second. Bigger fans and heat sinks became part of every computer.
facts: At 180 nm, a transistor is already thousands of times thinner than a hair.

chips.name: Dual-Core CPU
chips.story: Instead of running faster, chips began to add a second processor core so two jobs could run side by side.
facts: Speed gains now come from parallel work.

chips.name: Quad-Core CPU
chips.story: Four cores and 3D transistor shapes pushed performance up while holding power steady.
facts: Same power as 2006, many times the work.

chips.name: 2 nm-Class Processor
chips.story: An entire city of technology fits on a fingertip: tens of billions of switches that use less power than the chip before.
facts: 2 nm features are only a few dozen atoms wide.
